item.title: Dropping eBPF CPU Cost by About 90% With Memoization (Not AI Gen)
item.description:
My brother and I spent a lot of time designing our eBPF security agent to be really fast from the ground up, but recently we discovered we could make it much faster using memoization!

A couple of weeks ago, I profiled the eBPF code and found that the most expensive part of the protection isn’t actually enforcing a policy (allow/deny), but figuring out which policy applies to a given file open.

item.title: Optimizing eBPF Policies for Speed and Space (Not AI Gen)
item.description:
When writing our eBPF code, my brother and I wanted our policies to be extremely fast and space efficient, and we also wanted processes to inherit policies (while still being fast and space efficient). This blog post explains what we did to make our eBPF code fast.

This blog post is kind of long and dense, so to not keep you (the reader) on a weird cliffhanger, the short answer is “bitmasks”! I’m also pretty sure that my writing “bitmasks” just made the cliffhanger worse ;)
